title: Isthmus Peak Track: Wānaka area, Otago region
overview: Isthmus Peak Track is a steep and challenging but rewarding hike located between Lake Wānaka and Lake Hāwea, offering panoramic views of both lakes and the Southern Alps.
5 to 7 hr return from Isthmus Peak Track car park
November to December – Track annually closed for fawning between 20 November and 20 December.
March to May – Safari hunting takes place on Glen Dene Station. Be alert and stay visible, especially during the March to May roar hunting season.
No dogs. Other pets on conservation land rules.

5 to 7 hr return from Isthmus Peak Track car park
November to December – Track annually closed for fawning between 20 November and 20 December.
March to May – Safari hunting takes place on Glen Dene Station. Be alert and stay visible, especially during the March to May roar hunting season.
It is a steep and lengthy climb as you gain 1000 m over 8 km. Make sure you have sturdy hiking boots and plenty of water as there are no water sources along the track.
Isthmus Peak Track car park is off SH6, north of Lake Hāwea township and 30 minutes drive from Wanaka.
Avalanches can occur in any season. Any time that snow and steep slopes are combined there is potential for an avalanche. You need to understand the risks before you visit avalanche-prone country.
This area has terrain that can produce avalanches that cross the track, usually from May into November. View avalanche information and the terrain rating for this track .

You need permission from the Makarora River Ranch to take your dog into Hāwea Conservation Park using Boundary Creek Track. Email makaroraranch@gmail.com at least 24 hours in advance of your visit to request permission. You must provide a valid worming certificate to ensure your dog is free from hydatids and sheep measles.
Firearms are not permitted on this track.
